title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Penbrook Bank
meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-24 / Start: 14:00 PDT / Duration: 42 minutes / Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Penbrook CISO), David Chen (Penbrook Head of Cloud), Samantha Price (Penbrook PM)
summary: Weekly POC security sync. Reviewed SSO/SAML test plan, audit log retention and format, data retention during pilot, SOC 2 evidence and timeline. Agreed to run SAML test next week, share SOC 2 whitepaper and an anonymized audit-log sample. Discussed concerns about data residency and role-based access controls; Redwood to confirm KMS/HSM integrations and encryption at rest details.
topics: SSO / SAML test plan and metadata exchange
questions: What fields do audit logs include by default?
How quickly can log export be enabled to our SIEM?
Can we configure per-tenant retention during POC?
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC 2 whitepaper and current cert dates (by 2026-06-26)
Redwood: share sample anonymized audit log export and schema (by 2026-06-29)
Penbrook: provide SAML IdP metadata for staging env (by 2026-06-26)
Schedule security deep-dive if outstanding questions remain (tentative week of 2026-06-29)
action_items: Jared Kim: Email SOC 2 whitepaper and cert dates; due 2026-06-26
Priya Shah: Export anonymized audit log sample and upload to shared drive; due 2026-06-29
Marta Lopez: Share SAML IdP metadata and test users for staging; due 2026-06-26
David Chen: Confirm SIEM ingestion details and required formats; due 2026-06-30
transcript:
[00:00] Jared Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll get started. quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta Lopez: Marta here, CISO at Penbrook.
[00:08] David Chen: David, head of cloud.
[00:09] Samantha Price: Samantha, product manager.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood, SE on the pilot.
[00:15] Jared Kim: ok great, agenda is SSO, audit logs, data retention during pilot, and SOC 2 evidence. should take about 40 minutes.
[00:28] Marta Lopez: quick call out, we had a couple questions from legal about data residency and whether logs could contain PII during the pilot, so that's a main item.
[00:36] Priya Shah: totally makes sense. on the logs side, Redwood's audit logs include request metadata, model id, timestamp, user id (we can pseudonymize), and API key used; note some transcriptions may contain user-generated content so we recommend redaction rules on the client side.
[00:52] David Chen: can you confirm the fields again, like do we get full prompt text by default in the logs?
[00:57] Priya Shah: default export includes prompt hash and a snippet, not the full content unless you opt in. i'll double-check but current POC default is snippet + metadata, full text optional with explicit consent.
[01:10] Samantha Price: and retention during the pilot — we only want logs for 30 days and then auto-delete. is that configurable?
[01:16] Jared Kim: yes pilot retention can be configured per-tenant; we can set a 30-day TTL on logs for your staging account. we'll note that as an action.
[01:24] Marta Lopez: great. also SOC 2 — your security docs we saw were high level, but procurement wants scope dates and any recent gaps.
[01:32] Jared Kim: sure, i'll send the SOC 2 whitepaper and cert dates. quick note: Redwood's control environment is scoped to hosted infra for the hosted offering; for private deployments we do a different attestation path.
[01:47] David Chen: for the pilot we might be in hosted but behind a VPC peering setup, can you confirm network isolation?
[01:53] Priya Shah: yes for the dedicated/private options we support VPC peering or customer-managed VPC; for hosted we provide V-P-C connectors and egress controls. (laughs) sorry i said V-P-C — transcription sometimes writes it that way.
[02:05] Marta Lopez: is customer-managed KMS supported? we need to ensure keys are in our HSM.
[02:10] Priya Shah: yes we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and BYOK/HSM options for dedicated/private. for the hosted pilot we can enable CMK backing for data at rest; i'll confirm the exact HSM provider options in the follow-up.
[02:22] Samantha Price: for the SSO test — we provisioned a test IdP in our staging tenant, how fast can we do the SAML metadata exchange and smoke test?
[02:31] Jared Kim: usually same-week; priya can walk through the metadata fields now.
[02:35] Priya Shah: ok the minimum we need is entityID, sso URL, certificate (x509), and test user attributes (email, name, groups). we map groups to RBAC roles — admin, developer, viewer.
[02:48] Marta Lopez: do roles map automatically or do we need custom mapping?
[02:51] Priya Shah: there's a default mapping, you can set custom rules in the console; we support group->role mapping and attribute-based rules.
[02:58] David Chen: about audit logs to our SIEM — can we push logs via HTTPS forwarder or do you support S3 export?
[03:04] Priya Shah: both. we support real-time webhooks to an HTTPS endpoint, S3 export of daily batched logs, and direct SIEM connectors for Splunk/Datadog via our partner integrations. i'll include the formats in the sample.
[03:18] Samantha Price: is there PII redaction during export? we might need prompt redaction before logs leave the sandbox.
[03:24] Priya Shah: yes we have server-side redaction rules and client-side SDK helpers; strongly recommend client-side redaction for sensitive fields. for the POC we can enable server-side pseudonymization — again we'll provide config examples.
[03:36] Marta Lopez: on SOC 2 evidence, procurement asked for the last audit date, any exceptions, and the change log for infra changes in last 6 months. can you provide that?
[03:45] Jared Kim: yes i'll put those in the package, including any exception remediation notes. note that for customers on dedicated contracts we offer more granular audit logs and longer retention as part of enterprise add-ons.
[03:58] David Chen: one more thing — latency/cost tradeoffs. if we enable full request logging with full prompt text, is there any impact on performance or cost?
[04:06] Priya Shah: minimal runtime impact; it's mostly storage and egress costs. if you need high-throughput low-latency we recommend prefix caching and hashed logging to avoid storing full text.
[04:16] Samantha Price: for the next steps can we have a security deep-dive with our SREs and Penbrook security?
[04:22] Jared Kim: yes propose Wed 2026-06-30 or Thu 2026-07-01 afternoon, i'll follow up with calendar invites.
[04:29] Marta Lopez: sounds good.
[04:31] Priya Shah: i'll also capture a sample anonymized audit log and the schema — note the schema will have fields: timestamp, request_id, model_id, user_id_hash, prompt_snippet, action, outcome, region.
[04:45] Marta Lopez: ok please ensure user_id is hashed not plain.
[04:48] Priya Shah: yes hashed, and we can salt on your side if you prefer.
[04:52] David Chen: any blockers on SAML test? we can drop metadata into the shared folder after the call.
[04:57] Jared Kim: none, priya will run the test with you once we have metadata; action items noted.
[05:03] Samantha Price: procurement also asked about data deletion workflows when pilot ends — is there an API to purge?
[05:09] Priya Shah: yes deletion APIs and retention policies; we support immediate purge requests and automated TTL-based deletions. for hosted pilots we document the deletion SLA (usually 48-72 hours) and we'll include that in the follow-up.
[05:22] Marta Lopez: ok great. anything else?
[05:24] Jared Kim: quick recap of next steps: send SOC 2 docs, sample logs, SAML testing, schedule deep-dive. any objections?
[05:33] Marta Lopez: none from me.
[05:35] David Chen: all good.
[05:36] Samantha Price: good. thanks everyone.
[05:38] Jared Kim: thanks, we'll follow up. bye.
notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., V-P-C for VPC, K-V cash for KV cache).
Customer emphasized requirement for hashed user ids in logs and 30-day pilot retention.
